17.3.5 Preparation of Amines

Amines can be prepared by a number of different methods. Some of these are given below.

17.3.5.1 Alkylation of Ammonia by Alkyl halides

Ammonia is a very good nucleophile and will readily undergo alkylation when treated with an alkyl halide. When an alkyl halide is heated with alcoholic ammonia, it yields a mixture of primary, secondary, tertiary amines and quaternary ammonium salt. During this reaction the hydrogen atoms of ammonia are replaced by alkyl groups of alkyl halide, therefore, this reaction is also known as alkylation of ammonia. The reaction of ammonia with methyl iodide is given below.

If the quaternary ammonium salt is the desired product, then an excess of the alkyl halide is used.

17.3.5.2 Reduction of Nitrogen Containing Functional Groups

17.3.5.2.1 Reduction of Nitriles

When nitriles are reduced they yield the corresponding primary amines. This reduction can be brought about by hydrogen in the presence of catalyst such as Ni, Pt or Pd (catalytic hydrogenation) or by lithium aluminum hydride in ether, followed by workup.

17.3.5.2.2 Reduction of Nitroalkanes

Primary amines are prepared by the reduction of nitroalkanes with hydrogen in the presence of Ni or Pt or Pd catalyst. They can also be reduced by Fe or Sn in hydrochloric acid.

17.3.5.2.3 Reduction of Amides

Amines are obtained when amides are reduced by lithium aluminum hydride in ether. Primary, secondary and tertiary amides yield corresponding primary, secondary and tertiary amines respectively.

17.3.5.2 Reduction of Nitrogen Containing Functional Groups

17.3.5.2.1 Reduction of Nitriles

When nitriles are reduced they yield the corresponding primary amines. This reduction can be brought about by hydrogen in the presence of catalyst such as Ni, Pt or Pd (catalytic hydrogenation) or by lithium aluminum hydride in ether, followed by workup.

17.3.5.2.2 Reduction of Nitroalkanes

Primary amines are prepared by the reduction of nitroalkanes with hydrogen in the presence of Ni or Pt or Pd catalyst. They can also be reduced by Fe or Sn in hydrochloric acid.

17.3.5.2.3 Reduction of Amides

Amines are obtained when amides are reduced by lithium aluminum hydride in ether. Primary, secondary and tertiary amides yield corresponding primary, secondary and tertiary amines respectively.
